title: Sinensetin attenuates post-stroke depression via dual modulation of TLR4/NF-kappaB-NRF2/GPX4 pathways.
authors: Fan, Qiqi; Huang, Renfeng; Luo, Kunling; Chen, Jiaxin; Yin, Xuanying; Zhao, Erjuan; Liu, Yuanyue; Sheng, Lei; Wang, Qi; Cai, Weiwu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然化合物Sinensetin通过TLR4/NF-κB和NRF2/GPX4通路改善卒中后抑郁，虽含分子对接/MD模拟，但核心是药物-蛋白互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Post-stroke depression (PSD) is a complex neuropsychiatric complication driven by neuroinflammation and ferroptosis, yet effective therapies remain limited. Sinensetin (SIN), a polymethoxylated flavone derived from citrus fruits, possesses potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, its therapeutic efficacy and underlying mechanisms in PSD have not been explored. To investigate this, a mouse model of PSD was established by combining photothrombotic stroke with low-dose lipopolysaccharide (LPS) administration. Mice were treated with SIN (25 and 50 mg/kg) for 14 days. Depressive-like behaviors were assessed using the sucrose preference test (SPT), tail suspension test (TST), and forced swimming test (FST). Crucially, protein-level validation was performed using quantitative immunofluorescence (for glial activation) and ELISA (for serum cytokines and pathway markers), complemented by qPCR and molecular docking/dynamics (MD) simulations. SIN treatment significantly alleviated depressive-like behaviors and restored cerebral blood flow in PSD mice. Quantitative immunofluorescence and ELISA analyses revealed that SIN effectively suppressed the hyperactivation of microglia (IBA1) and astrocytes (GFAP) in the hippocampus and reduced serum concentrations of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta). Mechanistically, SIN inhibited the TLR4/NF-kappaB signaling pathway by suppressing NF-kappaB nuclear translocation and concurrently activated the NRF2/GPX4 antioxidant axis, thereby mitigating lipid peroxidation and neuronal ferroptosis. Additionally, molecular docking and MD simulations predicted energetically favorable interactions between SIN and key targets (e.g., TLR4, KEAP1), providing supportive evidence for its multi-target mechanism. Our findings demonstrate that SIN exerts neuroprotective effects in PSD by dually modulating TLR4/NF-kappaB-mediated neuroinflammation and NRF2/GPX4-dependent ferroptosis. These results highlight SIN as a promising natural therapeutic candidate for the treatment of depression following stroke.
abstract_zh: 卒中后抑郁（PSD）是一种由神经炎症和铁死亡驱动的复杂神经精神并发症，然而有效的治疗方法仍然有限。辛弗林素（SIN），一种源自柑橘类水果的多甲氧基黄酮，具有强效的抗炎和抗氧化特性。然而，其在PSD中的治疗效果及潜在机制尚未被探索。为研究此问题，通过结合光血栓性卒中与低剂量脂多糖（LPS）给药建立了PSD小鼠模型。小鼠接受SIN（25和50 mg/kg）治疗14天。使用蔗糖偏好测试（SPT）、悬尾测试（TST）和强迫游泳测试（FST）评估抑郁样行为。关键的是，通过定量免疫荧光（用于胶质细胞活化）和ELISA（用于血清细胞因子和通路标志物）进行了蛋白水平验证，并辅以qPCR和分子对接/动力学（MD）模拟。SIN治疗显著缓解了PSD小鼠的抑郁样行为并恢复了脑血流。定量免疫荧光和ELISA分析显示，SIN有效抑制了海马中小胶质细胞（IBA1）和星形胶质细胞（GFAP）的过度活化，并降低了促炎细胞因子（TNF-α、IL-6、IL-1β）的血清浓度。在机制上，SIN通过抑制NF-κB核转位来阻断TLR4/NF-κB信号通路，同时激活NRF2/GPX4抗氧化轴，从而减轻脂质过氧化和神经元铁死亡。此外，分子对接和MD模拟预测了SIN与关键靶点（如TLR4、KEAP1）之间能量上有利的相互作用，为其多靶点机制提供了支持性证据。我们的研究结果表明，SIN通过双重调节TLR4/NF-κB介导的神经炎症和NRF2/GPX4依赖的铁死亡，在PSD中发挥神经保护作用。这些结果凸显了SIN作为治疗卒中后抑郁的有前景的天然候选药物。
